claims.statement: `release.confirm` and `release.skip` are the only two declarations, and either one satisfies the release precondition; without one, `review.note` refuses to close the batch.

The release act is entered without spending an event once the four settle items are complete — the phase advances as an effect of `settlement.todo`, which is why release never appears as a payload of its own.
`review.note` is the single closing action: unarmed it settles the batch and increments `run.batch`; armed with `run.retire` it stamps the ending instead, and the same payload cannot do both.

The two-stage merge discipline — iteration integration on develop and the round-level develop→master merge — must never run in the same step, because a master merge before every feature has landed merges a state that was never verified end to end.

`develop` and `master` synchronise by reset only (`git reset --hard master` then `--force-with-lease`), never by rebasing develop or merging master back into it: the no-fast-forward topology is the rollback history.
The merge ritual ends with `git push origin master` and an unpushed trunk counts as an incomplete merge — a local merge that never reached origin is not a release.
Deployment accepts master refs only and every deployment is reported and approved before it runs; there is no override switch, because deployment is the one write that leaves this machine.

A Mod or host binary upgrade lands after settlement and starts a new run id — old run directories are never migrated or adopted, so a failed load is answered with a new run rather than a repair attempt.
